text:
claire: heads-up - ran a cross-model calibration experiment for speculative decoding tonight. setup: predictor=guide-4b-fp16, verifier=atlas-13b-q4g. Goal: fix verifier over-confidence on quant kernels to reduce false accepts on QA holdouts.

raj: nice. what calibration method did you try? temperature scaling or isotonic?

claire: started with temperature scaling on the verifier logits (single scalar per-quant-profile). also tried per-token logit shift for attention-fused kernels. Preliminary: temp=1.8 reduced accept_rate by ~8pts and cut QA EM regression from -3.2 -> -0.6 on knol-small.

emily: good sign. did you keep predictor unchanged?

claire: predictor unchanged (greedy guide-4b). eval command used:
```
./eval_harness \
  --predictor=guide-4b-fp16 \
  --verifier=atlas-13b-q4g \
  --spec_mode=cross_model \
  --verifier_temp=1.8 \
  --early_abort=0.10 \
  --tasks=qa,summarization \
  --holdouts=knol-small,summ-short-v1 \
  --batch=12
```
raj: metrics? accept_rate, paired-bootstrap pvals?

claire: accept_rate down from 71%->63% on knol-small. QA EM loss reduced to -0.6 (not sig), paired-bootstrap p=0.18. Summarization ROUGE-L unchanged within noise. Speedup dropped marginally (~1.95x -> 1.82x tokens/sec).

emily: so temp scaling helped but cost some perf. did you try per-quant-profile temps? q4g vs q4h etc?

claire: yes, per-profile temps found q4g needed 1.7 and q4h 2.0 on dev. applied per-profile scaling in runtime mapping and re-ran - small further quality gain, accept_rate more in line with fp16 verifier.

raj: any weird failure modes left? e.g., verifier accepting hallucinated short completions?

claire: still see some cases where predictor gives an overly concise factual string that verifier (post-temp) still accepts. Root cause seems calibration mismatch for cross-model tokenization differences. Added a post-accept heuristics: if verifier_accept and predicted_len < 12 and predictor_entropy < 1.1 -> force re-decode. That caught many false accepts on knol-small.

ops-bot: telemetry note: added metrics `verifier_temp_applied`, `accept_rate_by_quant_profile`, `short_pred_accepts_flagged`. Runtime will emit these for nightly.

emily: can you push branch and artifacts? I'll run longer paired bootstrap (n=2000) and a small qualitative triage of 50 regressed QA cases.

claire: branch pushed: git@repo:redwood/exp/crosscalib-spec-7777.git tag crosscalib-2026-03-21. Artifacts at /experiments/crosscalib-7777/. CI job queued for paired-bootstrap (job 7777003001).

ci-bot: job 7777003001 queued - logs: https://ci/internal/arty/7777003001 - artifacts: /artifacts/7777003001/metrics.json

raj: if bootstrap still shows residual QA delta, mitigation options: (1) increase verifier conservatism for knol tasks, (2) route knol->same-model speculative only, or (3) require ensemble-verifier for knowledge queries. We should weigh perf cost vs risk.

emily: agree. also let's add per-case accept_reason in logs so we can quickly filter "accepted due to high raw-score vs accepted after rescoring".

claire: adding accept_reason and per-case token-diff dumps to the artifacts. Next steps: wait for paired-bootstrap, run qualitative triage, then decide mitigations. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
